column1: # RECIPE_MEMORY.tsv - append-only lesson memory of qualification/hash-reentrant-guard-20261107: one row per lesson, appended in the same commit as the correction.

column4: measure the java.util twin before choosing between fail-fast and repair: under the same re-entrant callbacks HashMap answers reads with the pre-change value and is itself damaged in many mutating shapes, so throwing on every disturbed lookup would make M3 stricter than the JDK for reads while matching it nowhere it matters
column5: REFERENCE.tsv: HashMap BEFORE 99, AFTER 55, DAMAGED 57; the tree leaf (#2676) chose fail-fast without such a reference

column4: when the walk is the only reader of the structure, a disturbed walk can simply start again: the answer is the post-change state (linearizable), no exception; bound the restarts so a key whose equals mutates at every call cannot loop forever
column5: head: 0 WRONG, 0 DAMAGED and no new FAILFAST; mutant SM-9 (refuse at once) is killed by the strictness rule

column4: every extra lookup is another window for user callbacks: findSlot followed by put, and a second hashCode call in M3WeakHashMap.put, produced lost racing inserts and duplicate keys; one walk plus insertion by the walk's hash (locate/insertAbsent, java.util.HashMap's single-walk compute) closes them and also reduces the callback count; where a callback count is pinned by a contract test (M3WeakHashMap.put's second hashCode, M3FootprintContractTest), keep the call and look again when it changed the structure
column5: base: putIfAbsent/computeIfAbsent/compute/merge(new) WRONG 36 each, M3WeakHashMap duplicate key 9 DAMAGED; head: none

column4: encode the brief's 'not stricter than the JDK' as a test rule (FAILFAST accepted only where the twin is not cleanly linearizable), or a fail-fast mutant passes every oracle
column5: before the rule, REWALKS = 0 would have survived; with it SM-9 is killed

column4: a loop-shape change in a hot lookup can cost more than the check it carries: an outer retry loop around the probe loop measured 1.14-1.20 x base on Integer get/put; keeping the original probe loop and moving the retry into a cold method brought it back inside the A/A band
column5: BENCH.tsv and the bench2/bench3 runs recorded in GATES.tsv

column4: on a loaded desktop (85 % CPU) separate JVM forks per side gave A/A ratios from 0.76 to 1.02; alternate base and head rounds in one JVM through two class loaders and report the median paired ratio against an A/A run

M3LinkedHashMap and M3LinkedHashSet allocate through the m3_arrays JNI library even in tests; build it from m3/arrays/src/main/native with CMake + MinGW (the sparse checkout needs m3/native for m3_jni_core.h) and pass m3.arrays.native.path, else skip and name the owners
column5: the first measurement run died with UnsatisfiedLinkError in M3LinkedHashMap.createTable

column4: a write path no shape exercises keeps its mutant alive: merge on a present key with a non-null result had no shape, so SM-7 (merge writes through put again) survived until merge(write) was added
column5: MUTANTS.tsv: SM-7 KILLED after the shape

column4: run the JNI-gated (native profile) suite on base and head when a change touches owners the default suite skips: M3FootprintContractTest pins M3WeakHashMap.put's hashCode count and is excluded by default because it also builds an M3LinkedHashMap
column5: the default build passed 2142/2142 while the native suite failed 2 M3FootprintContractTest cases on the hash-once version; fixed by keeping the pinned call
